title: chrysolepis chrysophylla
intro: Chrysolepis chrysophylla, commonly known as the Santa Cruz cypress or golden chaparral huckleberry, is a species of flowering plant in the family Ericaceae. This shrub or small tree is native to the coniferous forests of the southwestern United States and northwestern Mexico. The plant has been traditionally used in herbal medicine for its health benefits, including anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, which may help alleviate conditions such as arthritis and digestive issues. Chrysolepis chrysophylla's therapeutic actions are attributed to its bioactive constituents, including flavonoids, phenolic acids, and triterpenoids, which may also exhibit antimicrobial and hepatoprotective effects.
